purpose: Full runtime safety knowledge supplied to SafeWork AI so it can infer job phases, hazards, controls, permits, competence, emergency needs and stop-work conditions from a plain-language job description.
reasoning_policy: Identify the intended job and expand it into a normal end-to-end work sequence without asking the user to list every step.
Treat inferred work methods as provisional and distinguish them from site facts confirmed by the user.
Use the full topic modules to identify hazards and controls across every inferred phase.
Ask only for material site-specific facts that cannot safely be inferred.
Never treat a generated assessment, method statement or permit as approved or issued.

topics.title: Dust, fume, mist and local exhaust ventilation
topics.purpose: Control airborne contaminants at source and determine when competent LEV design, testing, monitoring or RPE is needed.

intake_questions.question: What contaminant is generated, by which process, at what rate and close to which breathing zones?
Can the process be changed, enclosed, wetted or extracted at source?
What commissioning, indicator, examination, exposure-monitoring or health-surveillance evidence confirms control?

hazards.hazard: Inhalation of harmful airborne contaminant
control_prompts: clean by suitable vacuum or wet method
add suitable RPE for residual risk

competence_requirements: Competent LEV design, commissioning and examination
Competent exposure assessment where needed
ppe_considerations: RPE follows the PPE/RPE module
emergency_requirements: Stop process after extraction failure or uncontrolled release
health_surveillance_considerations: Respiratory or skin surveillance where risk criteria are met
stop_work_conditions: Contaminant identity or generation is unknown
Specified extraction is absent or ineffective
Unexpected visible dust, fume, odour, symptom or alarm occurs
topics.legal_currency_note: Verify current WELs, measurement strategy and LEV examination requirements.

topics.title: Asbestos-containing materials
topics.purpose: Prevent uncontrolled disturbance and route work to the correct survey, plan, competence and licensing decision.

intake_questions.question: What building or plant fabric will be disturbed, where and to what depth?
Is a suitable asbestos survey and register available for the exact work area and intrusive scope?
Has each suspect material been identified by competent survey or analysis?

hazards.hazard: Disturbance releases respirable asbestos fibres

competence_requirements: Asbestos awareness for those who may encounter ACMs
Task and licensing competence appropriate to classified work
ppe_considerations: RPE and protective clothing are selected only within a complete asbestos control plan
emergency_requirements: Stop, isolate area and follow accidental disturbance procedure
health_surveillance_considerations: Medical surveillance and records where legally applicable
stop_work_conditions: Survey does not cover the exact intrusive work
Suspect material is unidentified
Required licence, notification, plan, control or clearance is absent
topics.legal_currency_note: Classification of licensed, notifiable non-licensed and non-licensed work must use current HSE requirements.

topics.title: Biological agents and infection exposure
topics.purpose: Assess deliberate or incidental exposure to biological agents, contaminated materials, sharps, waste and bodily fluids.

intake_questions.question: What agent or contaminated source may be present, and is exposure deliberate or incidental?
Which routes are credible?
Could anyone be especially vulnerable because of health, pregnancy, immunity or age?

hazards.hazard: Exposure to infectious or sensitising biological material
control_prompts: provide ventilation where aerosol can arise
prohibit eating and drinking in contaminated area

competence_requirements: Workers trained in contamination control, hygiene, waste and exposure response
ppe_considerations: Select gloves, clothing, eye, face and respiratory protection for the agent, route and task
emergency_requirements: Needlestick, splash, bite, spill and exposure follow-up
Prompt medical advice where indicated
health_surveillance_considerations: Vaccination, health surveillance or occupational-health advice where the assessment identifies need
stop_work_conditions: Agent or contamination status is unknown and controls cannot cover the uncertainty
Containment, hygiene or waste arrangements fail
Unplanned exposure occurs
topics.legal_currency_note: Obtain agent- and sector-specific current public-health and occupational guidance.

topics.title: Confined spaces
topics.purpose: Identify confined spaces and specified risks, prioritise avoidance and require a complete safe system and rescue plan before entry.

intake_questions.question: Describe the enclosure, access, dimensions, contents, connected services and previous use.
Can the work be completed without entering the space?
Which specified risks or hazardous atmospheres could arise before or during work?
What rescue method, trained team, communications and equipment will be immediately available?

hazards.hazard: Oxygen deficiency or enrichment, toxic or flammable atmosphere
control_prompts: test atmosphere using suitable calibrated equipment

hazards.hazard: Inrush, engulfment, flooding, heat or restricted rescue

competence_requirements: Competent confined-space classification and planning
Trained entrants, top person and rescuers
Competent atmospheric testing
ppe_considerations: PPE and respiratory protection selected from measured conditions and rescue compatibility
emergency_requirements: A site-specific rescue plan that does not rely solely on the public emergency services
Recovery equipment and first-aid arrangements immediately available
health_surveillance_considerations: Fitness for the environment, PPE and task where appropriate
stop_work_conditions: Entry can be avoided but has not been
Isolations, permit, testing or rescue arrangements are incomplete
Atmosphere leaves agreed limits or communications fail
topics.legal_currency_note: Use the current Confined Spaces Regulations, ACOP and site requirements when deciding whether the space and risks are in scope.

topics.title: Dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
topics.purpose: Control fire, explosion and pressure effects from flammable, oxidising, explosive or pressurised substances and combustible dusts.

intake_questions.question: Which dangerous substances, quantities, release scenarios and physical properties are present?
Could an explosive atmosphere form, and has any hazardous area been classified?
Which electrical, mechanical, static, flame or hot-surface ignition sources could occur?

hazards.hazard: Ignition or energetic release

competence_requirements: Competent DSEAR assessment and hazardous-area expertise where relevant
ppe_considerations: Flame-resistant or anti-static PPE only where justified and compatible with the full control strategy
emergency_requirements: Alarm, evacuation, isolation and firefighting strategy
Information for responders
stop_work_conditions: Substance properties or inventory are unknown
Hazardous area or equipment suitability is unresolved
Leak, alarm or unplanned ignition source occurs
topics.legal_currency_note: Use a current DSEAR assessment and specialist hazardous-area standards where applicable.

topics.title: Display screen, office and home working
topics.purpose: Assess habitual display-screen work, workstation setup, work organisation, home conditions and remote communication.

intake_questions.question: Does the person use display-screen equipment daily for continuous periods of about an hour or more?
Which office, home or mobile workstations are used and have they been assessed?
Are there discomfort, visual, workload, isolation or break-pattern concerns?

hazards.hazard: Poor posture, prolonged static work, visual demand or unsuitable work organisation
control_prompts: adjust chair, screen and input devices

competence_requirements: Trained DSE assessor or competent support for complex needs
emergency_requirements: Home-worker contact and emergency arrangements proportionate to work
health_surveillance_considerations: Occupational-health or ergonomic referral for persistent symptoms
stop_work_conditions: Reported pain or disability needs are not addressed
Home or remote conditions create an immediate electrical, fire or personal-safety risk
topics.legal_currency_note: Confirm current DSE-user definitions and employer duties for each work location.

topics.title: Electrical safety and isolation
topics.purpose: Control electrical energy during use, installation, maintenance, testing and work near services.

intake_questions.question: What system, voltage, energy source and equipment are involved?
Can the work be completed with the system isolated and proved dead?
Who controls the isolation, lock-off, testing and return to service?

hazards.hazard: Contact with live parts or induced/stored energy
control_prompts: prove tester, prove dead, re-prove tester

hazards.hazard: Fault, overload, damaged equipment or arc event

competence_requirements: Electrical work and testing performed only by persons competent for the system and task
ppe_considerations: Arc-rated or insulating PPE only where justified by a competent assessment; never as the primary reason to work live
emergency_requirements: Safe emergency isolation
Do not touch a casualty until the supply is isolated
Electrical fire response
stop_work_conditions: Circuit or isolation point cannot be positively identified
Work dead is possible but live work is proposed without specific justification
Equipment is damaged, wet, incorrectly rated or tests fail
topics.legal_currency_note: Electrical technical standards, test requirements and authorisation rules must be confirmed for the installation and organisation.

topics.title: Environmental protection within RAMS
topics.purpose: Add proportionate controls for pollution, waste, nuisance, resource use and environmental receptors affected by the job.

intake_questions.question: Which drains, watercourses, soil, neighbours, habitats or other environmental receptors could be affected?
Which fuels, chemicals, wastes, dusts, emissions or contaminated materials will be stored or generated?
What containment, segregation, collection, disposal and emergency arrangements apply?

hazards.hazard: Release, poor waste control or nuisance affects environment or community

competence_requirements: Environmental competence proportionate to receptors and regulated waste
ppe_considerations: PPE selected for cleanup only after safe containment and response planning
emergency_requirements: Spill containment, notification and cleanup plan
stop_work_conditions: Environmental receptors or disposal route are unknown
Containment or spill response is unavailable
Unexpected contamination, protected feature or release is found
topics.legal_currency_note: Environmental permits, waste classifications and regulator requirements must be confirmed for the location and material.

topics.title: Excavation, ground disturbance and buried services
topics.purpose: Control service strikes, collapse, falls, water ingress, plant interaction and confined conditions during ground work.

intake_questions.question: What depth, dimensions, ground conditions, support method and duration are planned?
Are current plans, site markings, locating results and safe-digging methods available?
Who will inspect the excavation and after which events?

hazards.hazard: Contact with buried electrical, gas, water or communication service
control_prompts: prove services by safe trial holes

Complete service review, competent locating, marking and required authorisation before any ground disturbance, including extraction of existing posts/foundations and trial holes; establish segregation first.

hazards.hazard: Ground collapse, falling material, falls or plant entering excavation

competence_requirements: Competent service locating, excavation planning and inspection
ppe_considerations: PPE supports, but does not replace, service and collapse controls
emergency_requirements: Service-strike response
Collapse and rescue plan without unplanned entry
stop_work_conditions: Plans or locating results are missing or conflict
Ground support or safe access is inadequate
Unknown service, water ingress, movement or atmosphere is encountered
topics.legal_currency_note: Confirm current service-owner requirements, excavation inspection duties and confined-space classification.

topics.title: Fire, explosion and hot work
topics.purpose: Identify ignition, fuel and oxygen interactions and control hot work, flammables, evacuation and fire watch arrangements.

intake_questions.question: Which flames, sparks, hot surfaces, electrical or static ignition sources will be present?
Which flammable liquids, gases, dusts, wastes, structures or hidden combustibles could be affected?
Will detection, alarms, suppression, compartmentation or escape routes be impaired?

hazards.hazard: Ignition of flammable or combustible material
control_prompts: fire watch during and after work

hazards.hazard: Ignition in a flammable atmosphere or combustible dust cloud

competence_requirements: Hot-work operator competence
Permit issuer understands the location, fire systems and hidden spread routes
ppe_considerations: Heat, flame, eye and respiratory protection selected for the process and nearby persons
emergency_requirements: Alarm raising and evacuation
Fire watch duration and handback
Cylinder emergency arrangements
health_surveillance_considerations: Consider fume exposure under the hazardous-substances module
stop_work_conditions: Permit controls are incomplete
Combustibles cannot be removed or protected
Fire system impairment is unauthorised
Gas leak, alarm or uncontrolled fume occurs
topics.legal_currency_note: Confirm site fire-risk assessment, insurer rules and permit requirements before work.

topics.title: First aid, emergency response and rescue
topics.purpose: Match first-aid and emergency arrangements to the workforce, location, hazards, response time and rescue needs.

intake_questions.question: Which credible emergencies could occur and what immediate actions are required?
What first-aid personnel, equipment, facilities and response times are needed for the work and workforce?
Could anyone become suspended, trapped, contaminated, unconscious or otherwise unable to self-rescue?

hazards.hazard: Emergency response or rescue is delayed, improvised or exposes rescuers

competence_requirements: First-aid and rescue competence proportionate to hazards
ppe_considerations: Responder PPE and contamination control
emergency_requirements: This module defines emergency arrangements for all RAMS
health_surveillance_considerations: Post-exposure medical and occupational-health follow-up
stop_work_conditions: Required first-aid cover is absent
A credible rescue need has no workable plan
Emergency access, alarm or communications are unavailable
topics.legal_currency_note: First-aid needs and specialist rescue arrangements must reflect current guidance and actual response capability.

topics.title: Fuel gas installation and appliances
topics.purpose: Control gas release, combustion products, fire, explosion and unsafe appliance work.

intake_questions.question: Which fuel, supply, appliance, pressure, ventilation and flue arrangements are involved?
Is the person legally competent and registered for the exact gas work category?
How will the supply be isolated, tested, purged and safely recommissioned?

hazards.hazard: Fuel gas release or incomplete combustion

competence_requirements: Current legal registration and competence for the appliance, fuel and work category
emergency_requirements: Gas-escape response, evacuation and emergency service contact
Carbon-monoxide response
stop_work_conditions: Competence category is not confirmed
Isolation, ventilation or flue condition is unsafe
Gas smell, alarm, failed test or suspected combustion-product release occurs
topics.legal_currency_note: Gas work must comply with current Gas Safety law and registration requirements.

topics.title: Hazardous substances and occupational exposure
topics.purpose: Route COSHH-style questions for substances, dusts, fumes, vapours, gases and exposure controls.

intake_questions.question: Which products, process-generated substances, dusts, fumes or biological contaminants may be present?
Are current safety data sheets and product labels available?
Which exposure routes are credible?
What quantity is used, for how long, how often and in what ventilation conditions?

hazards.hazard: Exposure to hazardous substance
control_prompts: select RPE/PPE only after higher controls

hazards.hazard: Spill, leak, incompatible mixing or loss of containment
Wood dust generated by cutting, drilling or sanding timber
control_prompts: Confirm timber and treatment type; do not assume hardwood
Avoid or minimise on-site cutting; use suitable on-tool extraction for dusty cutting/sanding
Segregate others and use appropriate vacuum or wet cleaning, not dry sweeping
Select RPE for residual exposure; tight-fitting RPE requires wearer-specific face-fit testing and an effective seal
Assess exposure and health-surveillance needs; absence of visible dust or symptoms does not demonstrate safe exposure

competence_requirements: Users understand product and process hazards, controls and emergency actions
Face-fit testing where tight-fitting RPE is selected
ppe_considerations: Select chemical compatibility, protection factor and wear time from the assessment
Check PPE does not introduce heat, visibility or dexterity risks
emergency_requirements: Spill and exposure response
Eyewash or emergency washing where justified
First-aid information accessible
health_surveillance_considerations: Consider where exposure can cause an identifiable disease or adverse effect and surveillance is appropriate
stop_work_conditions: Substance identity or SDS is unknown
Required extraction or RPE is unavailable
Unplanned odour, dust, symptoms, spill or alarm occurs
topics.legal_currency_note: Verify current workplace exposure limits and substance-specific duties against the latest authoritative EH40/HSE information.

topics.title: Incident, near-miss and statutory reporting
topics.purpose: Support immediate response, evidence preservation, proportionate investigation and escalation for potential statutory reporting.

intake_questions.question: Is anyone injured, exposed or in need of urgent medical help?
Has the area been made safe without destroying necessary evidence?
What happened, when, where, to whom and during which work step?

hazards.hazard: Uncontrolled scene causes further harm
Investigation focuses on blame or misses underlying causes

competence_requirements: Investigation level and team competence proportionate to potential severity
ppe_considerations: Responders use PPE suitable for remaining hazards
emergency_requirements: Emergency response takes priority over evidence collection
Escalate possible statutory reports to the responsible person promptly
health_surveillance_considerations: Arrange occupational-health follow-up after relevant exposure
stop_work_conditions: The scene remains unsafe
A serious control failure is not understood
Required regulator or emergency-service instructions have not been followed
topics.legal_currency_note: RIDDOR categories, definitions and reporting timescales must always be verified against current HSE guidance.

topics.title: Lead exposure
topics.purpose: Identify lead-containing materials and route exposure prevention, control, hygiene, monitoring and medical surveillance.

intake_questions.question: Which material may contain lead and how has its composition been confirmed?
Will work create dust, fume, ingestion risk or skin contamination?
What exposure assessment, hygiene, monitoring and medical-surveillance arrangements apply?

hazards.hazard: Inhalation or ingestion of lead
control_prompts: control dust or fume at source

competence_requirements: Competent lead exposure assessment and occupational-health support
ppe_considerations: Suitable RPE, clothing and gloves for residual exposure with controlled changing and cleaning
emergency_requirements: Response to uncontrolled contamination or significant exposure
health_surveillance_considerations: Medical surveillance and biological monitoring where legally required
stop_work_conditions: Lead status is unknown
Dust/fume and hygiene controls are inadequate
Required medical surveillance or exposure monitoring is absent
topics.legal_currency_note: Lead has its own regulatory regime and must not be assessed only under generic COSHH logic.

topics.title: Legionella and water-system hygiene
topics.purpose: Route water systems that can support and disseminate legionella to competent assessment, control schemes and monitoring.

intake_questions.question: What water system, temperatures, storage, outlets, aerosol sources and susceptible users are involved?
Is a current legionella risk assessment and written control scheme available?
Who is responsible for monitoring, maintenance, flushing, cleaning and corrective action?

hazards.hazard: Inhalation of contaminated water aerosol
control_prompts: design out stagnation and favourable temperatures

competence_requirements: Named responsible person and competent water-hygiene support
ppe_considerations: Task-specific protection for cleaning chemicals and aerosols
emergency_requirements: Response to control failure, positive result or suspected case
health_surveillance_considerations: Medical advice following relevant symptoms or exposure
stop_work_conditions: Risk assessment or control scheme is absent
Critical monitoring is outside control
System opening or aerosol work is unplanned
topics.legal_currency_note: Use the current L8/HSG274 framework and system-specific competence.

topics.title: Lifting operations and lifting equipment
topics.purpose: Require competent planning, suitable equipment, stable setup, controlled load paths and examination evidence for lifting work.

intake_questions.question: What is the verified load weight, shape, centre of gravity, lifting points and destination?
Which lifting appliance and accessories will be used, with what capacities and examination status?
Describe ground, weather, obstructions, load path, exclusion zone and communication method.

hazards.hazard: Load falls, swings, overturns equipment or strikes a person
control_prompts: control load path and exclusion zone
supervise and stop in unsafe conditions

competence_requirements: Competent lift planner, operator, slinger/signaller and supervisor appropriate to lift complexity
ppe_considerations: Head, hand, foot and visibility PPE for residual exposure
emergency_requirements: Plan for equipment failure, stranded load and contact with services
stop_work_conditions: Load weight or lifting points are unknown
Equipment certification or capacity is unverified
Ground, weather, communication or exclusion arrangements are unsafe
topics.legal_currency_note: Confirm current LOLER scope, thorough-examination requirements and any industry lifting standard.

topics.title: Lone working
topics.purpose: Determine whether work can be done alone and provide proportionate communication, monitoring and emergency support.

intake_questions.question: Is the task legally and practically suitable for one person to perform alone?
Where will the person be, who knows their itinerary and how will reliable contact be maintained?
What happens after a missed check-in, alarm, injury, violence or communication failure?

hazards.hazard: Injury or illness with delayed discovery and assistance
control_prompts: avoid lone work for high-risk tasks
use reliable communication or monitored alarm

hazards.hazard: Violence, intimidation or unsafe location

competence_requirements: Lone worker and monitor understand check-in, alarm and escalation procedures
ppe_considerations: Personal alarms or tracking devices are communication controls, not PPE
emergency_requirements: Time-bound missed-contact escalation with named responders
Location and access information available to responders
health_surveillance_considerations: Consider medical conditions only through a proportionate, confidential fitness assessment
stop_work_conditions: The task requires immediate assistance or rescue that cannot be provided
Communication or monitoring fails
Location or person presents an unassessed violence risk
topics.legal_currency_note: Confirm sector-specific prohibitions, client rules and safeguarding requirements.

topics.title: Machinery, work equipment and hand-held tools
topics.purpose: Control dangerous moving parts, ejected material, tool failure, energy and unsafe use or maintenance.

intake_questions.question: Identify each machine or tool, its task, power source, attachments and operating environment.
How are dangerous parts prevented from being reached during operation, clearing and maintenance?
What pre-use, statutory and maintenance inspections apply, and are records current?

hazards.hazard: Contact with moving parts, trapping points or cutting surfaces
control_prompts: then interlocked or adjustable guards and protective devices
provide safe feed and handling aids

hazards.hazard: Unexpected start-up or release of stored energy
Tool, workpiece or abrasive failure and ejection

competence_requirements: Operators trained and authorised for the equipment
Maintenance performed by competent persons
ppe_considerations: Eye, face, hearing, respiratory, hand, foot and body protection selected for residual risks
Avoid loose clothing, jewellery or unsuitable gloves near entanglement hazards
emergency_requirements: Accessible emergency stop where appropriate
Isolation and first-aid response
health_surveillance_considerations: Route noise, vibration, dust, fume and skin exposures to their specialist modules
stop_work_conditions: Guard or safety device is missing, defeated or defective
Tool or accessory is incompatible or damaged
Isolation cannot be secured and verified
topics.legal_currency_note: Confirm equipment-specific legal, inspection and manufacturer requirements.

topics.title: Health, safety, quality and environmental management systems
topics.purpose: Connect task controls to policy, responsibilities, competence, consultation, monitoring and continual improvement.

intake_questions.question: Who has authority to approve, supervise and stop this work?
Which client, principal contractor or site procedures apply?
How have workers and relevant contractors been consulted about the task?

hazards.hazard: Unclear roles or conflicting instructions
Work changes without reassessment

competence_requirements: Named competent reviewer
Supervisor understands the RAMS and site rules
emergency_requirements: Define reporting and escalation responsibilities
stop_work_conditions: Accountability is unclear
Site rules conflict with the proposed method
Material conditions or scope change
topics.legal_currency_note: Verify current standards, certification claims and legal duties before relying on dated course material.

topics.title: Manual handling and musculoskeletal health
topics.purpose: Avoid hazardous handling and assess the task, load, individual capability and environment where handling remains.

intake_questions.question: Can the load or process be changed so manual handling is avoided?
What are the load's weight, dimensions, stability, grip points and centre of gravity?
Describe the route, height, reach, twisting, frequency, duration and team involvement.

hazards.hazard: High force, awkward posture, repetition or fatigue
Dropped, unstable or shifting load

competence_requirements: Workers instructed in the specific handling plan and correct use of aids
ppe_considerations: Foot and hand protection may reduce consequence but do not make an unsafe lift acceptable
emergency_requirements: First-aid and reporting arrangements for pain or injury
health_surveillance_considerations: Early reporting and occupational-health referral for symptoms where appropriate
stop_work_conditions: Load details or route are unknown
Required handling aid is unavailable or defective
Worker reports pain or cannot complete the handling safely
topics.legal_currency_note: Do not use a single weight limit as proof of safety; assess the full handling operation and individual factors.

topics.title: Monitoring, audit and management review
topics.purpose: Define how controls, incidents, inspections and actions are checked after paperwork is issued.

intake_questions.question: Who will inspect the work and at what frequency?
What evidence will show that each critical control is working?
Which events or changes will trigger immediate review?

hazards.hazard: Controls exist on paper but are not implemented

competence_requirements: Auditors and inspectors understand the activity and remain sufficiently independent
emergency_requirements: Escalate serious control failure immediately
health_surveillance_considerations: Use anonymised trend information to review exposure controls
stop_work_conditions: A critical control fails
Inspection identifies imminent danger
Required corrective action is overdue and exposure continues
topics.legal_currency_note: Retention periods and statutory inspection intervals must be checked for the specific equipment and activity.

topics.title: Noise and vibration
topics.purpose: Assess noise, hand-arm vibration and whole-body vibration from tools, machinery, vehicles and work patterns.

intake_questions.question: Which equipment is used and what reliable noise or vibration data is available for the real operating condition?
How long and how often will each person use or work near the equipment?
Has anyone reported hearing difficulty, tingling, numbness, blanching, pain or back symptoms?

hazards.hazard: Harmful noise exposure or interference with communication
control_prompts: provide suitable hearing protection and information

hazards.hazard: Hand-arm or whole-body vibration
control_prompts: improve seats, suspension and travel surfaces

competence_requirements: Users trained in correct equipment selection, technique, defect reporting and exposure controls
ppe_considerations: Hearing protection selected for the exposure without excessive over-protection
Gloves are not treated as a substitute for vibration control
emergency_requirements: Stop and report sudden abnormal noise, vibration or equipment damage
health_surveillance_considerations: Audiometry where risk indicates
HAVS surveillance where workers are exposed at levels or conditions requiring it
stop_work_conditions: Exposure cannot be estimated from reliable data
Required controls or surveillance arrangements are absent
Symptoms are reported or equipment vibration/noise changes unexpectedly
topics.legal_currency_note: Verify current exposure action and limit values and calculation methods against current HSE guidance.

topics.title: Personal and respiratory protective equipment
topics.purpose: Select, issue, fit, use, maintain and replace PPE only for residual risks after higher-order controls.

intake_questions.question: Which residual hazard remains after elimination, substitution and engineering controls?
Is the equipment adequate for the hazard and suitable for the wearer, task, duration and environment?
How will issue, fit, compatibility, training, inspection, cleaning, storage and replacement be controlled?

hazards.hazard: Incorrect, incompatible, poorly fitted or badly maintained PPE
control_prompts: account for wear time and communication

For tight-fitting RPE: competent wearer-specific make/model/size face-fit test, fit check each use, clean-shaven seal area, compatible PPE, user training, maintenance and replacement. If no adequate seal is possible, assess suitable alternatives such as a loose-fitting powered hood.

competence_requirements: Competent PPE/RPE selection and face-fit testing where applicable
ppe_considerations: This module governs all PPE decisions
emergency_requirements: PPE must not be used to justify entry into an atmosphere requiring specialist breathing apparatus and rescue planning
health_surveillance_considerations: Consider wearer medical suitability where equipment imposes physiological load
stop_work_conditions: Higher-order controls have not been considered
Required protection level or compatibility is unknown
Fit, condition, training or replacement arrangements are inadequate
topics.legal_currency_note: Use current PPE duties and HSE RPE selection and face-fit guidance.

topics.title: Pressure systems and stored fluid energy
topics.purpose: Prevent uncontrolled release from compressed air, steam, gas, hydraulic and other pressure systems.

intake_questions.question: What fluid, pressure, temperature, volume and components form the system?
Does the system require a written scheme of examination, and is examination current?
How will pressure and stored mechanical energy be isolated, discharged and verified?

hazards.hazard: Rupture, hose failure, ejection or uncontrolled pressure release
control_prompts: exclude persons from line of fire

competence_requirements: System-specific competent person for examination and maintenance
ppe_considerations: PPE selected for residual fluid, temperature and injection risks
emergency_requirements: Emergency isolation and release response
Urgent medical response for injection injury
stop_work_conditions: Pressure, contents or system boundary is unknown
Required written scheme or examination is absent
Isolation and zero-pressure verification cannot be achieved
topics.legal_currency_note: A competent person must determine PSSR scope and written-scheme requirements.

topics.title: Ionising and non-ionising radiation
topics.purpose: Identify radiation sources and require specialist classification, exposure control and authorisation where applicable.

intake_questions.question: What source, wavelength or radionuclide is present, and what output, activity or classification applies?
Has the relevant radiation protection or laser safety adviser defined the controls?
Could exposure occur externally, through the eyes or skin, or through contamination and intake?

hazards.hazard: Exposure to ionising or harmful non-ionising radiation
control_prompts: monitor exposure or contamination as specified

competence_requirements: Specialist advice and trained authorised users appropriate to the source
ppe_considerations: PPE selected by specialist assessment; ordinary eyewear or clothing must not be assumed adequate
emergency_requirements: Source loss, exposure, contamination and equipment-failure procedures
health_surveillance_considerations: Medical surveillance and dose records where required by the specialist assessment and law
stop_work_conditions: Source or classification is unknown
Required specialist advice, shielding, monitoring or authorisation is absent
Interlock, enclosure or warning system fails
topics.legal_currency_note: Radiation work requires source-specific current legal and specialist advice; generic RAMS content is insufficient.

topics.title: Risk assessment and control selection
topics.purpose: Provide the common hazard-identification, risk-evaluation and control workflow used by every assessment.

intake_questions.question: What exactly will be done, in what sequence and what is outside the scope?
Who could be affected, including other trades, visitors and the public?
What controls are already in place and how will their effectiveness be confirmed?

hazards.hazard: Generic or incomplete assessment
Over-reliance on instructions or PPE
control_prompts: then add administrative controls and suitable PPE

competence_requirements: Assessment completed and approved by people competent for the task and hazards
ppe_considerations: PPE selection follows, and does not replace, higher-order controls
emergency_requirements: Consider foreseeable abnormal events as well as normal work
health_surveillance_considerations: Identify exposures for which health surveillance may be appropriate or required
stop_work_conditions: Mandatory task information is missing
Residual risk remains high or very high
Controls are unavailable or cannot be verified
topics.legal_currency_note: The assessment must be suitable and sufficient for the actual work and reviewed when circumstances change.

topics.title: Safe isolation and permit-to-work control
topics.purpose: Coordinate high-risk work through verified isolations, defined boundaries, authorisation, handover and controlled return to service.

intake_questions.question: Which electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, thermal, chemical, gravitational or process energies require control?
What isolation standard, locks, tags, blanks, restraints and proving method apply?

emergency_requirements: Permit suspension and emergency override process

Energy cannot be proved controlled
Permit conditions or work party change without re-authorisation
topics.legal_currency_note: The organisation's permit system and plant-specific isolation standard control the detailed procedure.

provide clean rest and eating arrangements

competence_requirements: Clear responsibility for housekeeping, inspection and defect response
ppe_considerations: Footwear selected for the surface and contamination after source controls
emergency_requirements: Keep emergency routes and welfare access unobstructed

Lighting, ventilation or temperature creates immediate danger
Basic welfare needed for the work is absent

topics.title: Work-related stress, mental health, substance misuse and violence

topics.title: Work at height

control_prompts: provide guardrails or other collective protection
use personal restraint or arrest only where higher controls are unsuitable

hazards.hazard: Tools or materials fall

competence_requirements: Planning, assembly, inspection and use by competent persons appropriate to the equipment
ppe_considerations: Harness, lanyard and connectors form a compatible system with suitable anchor and clearance
emergency_requirements: Rescue plan where a person could remain suspended or inaccessible
Do not rely only on the fire and rescue service
health_surveillance_considerations: Consider fitness where balance, medical condition or PPE use could affect safety
stop_work_conditions: Work at height can reasonably be avoided
Equipment, anchor or inspection is unverified
Weather, surface or edge conditions are unsafe

topics.title: Temporary traffic management for street works and road works
topics.purpose: Plan, install, inspect, maintain and remove temporary traffic management that protects workers and every road user, including pedestrians, cyclists, equestrians and disabled people.

intake_questions.question: What are the road type, speed limit, carriageway and footway widths, visibility, traffic flows, vulnerable-user routes, work dimensions and planned duration?

Who prepared and approved the temporary traffic-management layout, and what are its drawing number, revision, highway-authority permit or notice, road-space booking and any traffic-order or signal approval references?
Who will competently install, inspect, maintain, alter and remove the layout, and how will inspections, defects, changes and handback be recorded?
How will a continuous, accessible and clearly signed route be maintained for pedestrians, wheelchair and mobility-scooter users, people with pushchairs, cyclists and other vulnerable road users?

Will the job use portable two-way or multi-way signals, Stop/Go control, a lane or full road closure, a signed diversion, or more than one traffic-management phase? Give the approved settings, closure limits, phase sequence, changeover method and authority references.

application_rules: Use the Safety at Street Works and Road Works Code of Practice, commonly called the Red Book, for standard signing, lighting and guarding arrangements only where the road and site conditions fall within its scope and match the selected standard layout.

The Red Book applies to highways and roads other than motorways and dual carriageways with a speed limit of 50 mph or more. Use a competent site-specific Chapter 8 design where the Red Book does not apply or its standard layouts do not fit the actual conditions.

Use Traffic Signs Manual Chapter 8 Part 1 for temporary traffic-management design, Part 2 for planning and operational implementation, maintenance and removal, and Part 3 for current update guidance including TSRGD 2016 integration, diversions, speed limits, works length and spacing, sign clutter and designer competence.

Do not invent sign distances, cone spacing, taper lengths, safety-zone dimensions, signal timings or carriageway widths. Record the values from the approved layout and current guidance after a competent person has assessed the actual road.

Confirm the current highway-authority permit or notice, road-space booking and any required temporary traffic regulation order, temporary restriction, parking suspension or portable-signal approval before issue.

A traffic marshal or banksman supports controlled movements but does not replace signing, guarding, physical segregation or an approved traffic-management layout and must not direct public traffic unless competent and authorised to do so.
High-visibility clothing supports visibility but does not replace safe clearances, barriers, safety zones or separation from traffic.

Install and remove traffic-management equipment using a planned safe sequence from protected positions; maintain emergency access and do not expose workers while placing or retrieving signs and devices.

Inspect the layout after installation, at suitable recorded intervals, after alteration, impact, severe weather or reported defect, and before handback. Correct defects promptly and record the action.

For portable signals, record the number of approaches, controller and signal IDs, approved timing or design reference, detection or manual-control mode, commissioning checks, queue monitoring, fault response and competent-person acceptance. Do not invent signal timings.

For a full or partial road closure, record the exact limits, current order or notice and permit references, closure points, authorised and emergency access, the approved diversion route and signs, stakeholder communications, inspections and final handback.

For multi-phase or staged traffic management, identify every phase by drawing and revision, record its work limits and road-user routes, and use a briefed changeover sequence that establishes a safe temporary state, removes or covers conflicting signs and inspects the complete new layout before traffic is released.
required_records: approved traffic-management drawing number and revision
road and site data including speed limit, widths, visibility and work limits
highway-authority permit, notice, booking, order and signal references as applicable
sign, cone, barrier, lamp and signal schedule
taper, safety-zone, working-space and pedestrian-route dimensions taken from the approved layout
installation, alteration, shift and post-event inspection log
designer, installer, supervisor and highway or client contact details
installation handover and final removal or road handback signatures
portable-signal commissioning, settings, inspection, fault and removal record where used
road-closure authority, access, diversion inspection and handback record where used
multi-phase layout register and signed changeover log where used

hazards.hazard: Workers or road users enter an inadequately protected work area
A diversion or obstruction exposes a vulnerable road user to traffic, a fall, an inaccessible route or confusing information

competence_requirements: Temporary traffic-management design, installation, maintenance, inspection and removal by people competent for the road category and system used
Named supervisor with authority to stop work and correct defects
ppe_considerations: Suitable high-visibility clothing for the road environment, selected after higher-order traffic controls
emergency_requirements: Maintain emergency-service access and provide a method to make the site safe after collision, failed signals, displaced equipment or sudden deterioration
health_surveillance_considerations: Consider fatigue, night work, noise and exhaust exposure for traffic-management operatives
stop_work_conditions: No approved layout or the actual road conditions do not match it
Required authority, road-space, restriction or signal approval is absent
Signs, barriers, lamps, signals, tapers or safety zones are missing, displaced or defective
A safe accessible route for vulnerable road users cannot be maintained
Visibility, traffic, weather or site changes make the arrangement unsafe
topics.legal_currency_note: Check the live Department for Transport publications, current legislation and the relevant highway authority's requirements before issuing the pack. The generated record does not approve a traffic-management design or grant road-space permission.

emergency_requirements: Collision, breakdown and lone-driver arrangements
Electric-vehicle incident information for responders

professional_language.title: NEBOSH power words and professional language
professional_language.purpose: Help SafeWork AI use precise professional health and safety language in answers, risk assessments and RAMS without forcing terminology or overstating legal conclusions.
usage_rules: Use these terms naturally where they accurately describe the evidence, hazard, risk, control or outcome.
Prefer specific statements that identify the source of harm, people exposed, foreseeable consequences and effective control measures.
Distinguish a hazard from risk, initial risk from residual risk, and acute injury from chronic health effects.
Describe controls in hierarchy order and distinguish engineering controls, collective protection, administrative controls and PPE.
Use legal or enforcement terms only when the applicable law and facts support them; training language does not establish legal compliance.
Do not insert power words merely for style, repeat them unnecessarily or use them to imply that a draft RAMS is approved.
